tools.description: Search entities by name/IRI fragment across the loaded ontologies. 'type' is one of class, object_property, data_property, annotation_property, individual, datatype, all (default all). A plain fragment matches as a substring and '*' is a wildcard; an empty or wildcard-only query lists the active ontology's whole signature. Results are RANKED and synonym-aware: standard RDFS/SKOS/OBO lexical properties plus project-policy overrides are searched, and every hit explains score, source, matched value/property, language, normalization, collision, and review status. Paginated: 'limit' caps the page and 'offset' skips that many ranked hits — when the result carries 'next_offset', pass it back as 'offset' for the next page. 'best_match' is a guaranteed IRI ground; fuzzy/synonym 'reuse_candidate' values require review and never suppress minting. 'would_mint' is true only for a novel single term, while an exact preferred-name collision sets 'mint_blocked_by_collision' instead of choosing a winner. Large lexical expansions are bounded and report the omitted count.

tools.description: Save the active ontology to disk. With no arguments it writes to the ontology's existing document; a never-saved (untitled) ontology has no file yet, so pass 'path' to choose one (save-as). The serialization format is inferred from the file extension (.ttl/.turtle, .owl/.rdf/.xml, .omn, .ofn/.fss, .owx, .obo — anything else is an error); a path without an extension keeps the ontology's current format. After a save-as the ontology is bound to that file, so later argument-less saves go to the same place. Pass all=true to instead save EVERY ontology with unsaved changes to its own existing document (list_ontologies shows which are dirty). When the chosen format cannot represent the ontology without loss (an OBO term carrying more than one single-valued frame tag — name/comment/definition) the result carries a 'lossy_format_warning' and an 'obo_compatibility' report by default; set on_lossy=fail to refuse before writing instead (error_code=lossy_format_refused). For a fail-closed artifact pipeline set verify_round_trip=true: it writes beside the target, reloads without fetching the import closure, compares ontology id/direct imports/ontology and axiom annotations/normalized asserted axioms, reports round_trip.round_trip_class (byte_for_byte or axiom_identical), rejects anonymous individuals whose blank-node ids cannot survive reload, rechecks the live revision, and only then replaces the target. atomic=true requires an atomic filesystem move; backup=true preserves the previous artifact as <path>.bak.

all.description: Save every dirty ontology to its existing document instead of just the active one (default false; cannot be combined with 'path' — ontologies without a file are reported as skipped).

atomic.description: Require atomic target replacement; implies verify_round_trip.

backup.description: Copy an existing target to <path>.bak before replacement; implies verify_round_trip.

on_lossy.description: How to handle a target format that cannot represent the ontology without loss (default warn): 'warn' still saves and adds lossy_format_warning/obo_compatibility to the result; 'fail' refuses before writing with error_code=lossy_format_refused and leaves the target unchanged. Applies to a single-ontology save (ignored with all=true).

path.description: Optional file path to save to (save-as), e.g. /tmp/pets.ttl.

policy_bootstrap.description: Explicitly requested invalid-policy bootstrap for THIS save (default false). When the DISCOVERED project policy is loaded but still invalid (e.g. its declared root_artifact does not exist yet), a normal explicit-path save is refused fail-closed; with policy_bootstrap=true the save is instead authorized by the same containment-only rule as the documented import-lock bootstrap — capability-checked and confined to the invalid policy's canonical project_root, with filesystem.allow_external_paths deliberately NOT honored — so the policy-referenced artifact (e.g. the root_artifact) can be created at all. Requires an explicit 'path'. The result records what happened under 'policy_bootstrap' (used=true with the invalid policy's path and error codes, or used=false when the policy was valid/absent and normal authorization applied).

verify_round_trip.description: Use a temporary isolated reload and normalized document comparison before replacing the target; imports are not fetched and anonymous individuals are unsupported (default false for compatibility).

tools.description: Normalize a batch of structured axiom operations, apply the exact delta only to a private ontology snapshot, and run policy/default QC before any live edit. With no policy, the default gate includes the reasoner stage whenever a reasoner is selected: inconsistency or ANY unsatisfiable class in the changed snapshot blocks the commit (the same result-state semantics used by apply_changes verify=report|rollback; pass explicit gates to override). satisfiability_checked=false in the result means no reasoner verdict gated this preview. tools.description: Deterministically re-resolve a cached change-set preview against the current ontology revision. Read-only: the live ontology is never modified. When every original request position re-resolves to exactly the same axioms, a NEW preview change set is created at the current base revision with a fresh isolated preflight, and the original preview is kept until discarded or expired (discard it after committing the rebased one). When any referenced name now resolves to a different IRI, an operand newly fails to resolve, or a minted IRI is not deterministic (auto-generated ID preferences), the rebase fails closed with error_code=rebase_conflict listing the differing positions plus both complete revision envelopes for human review — a revision mismatch is never auto-merged. Previews from preview_change_set, create_terms preview=true, and create_properties preview=true are all rebasable, and the original request's gates/timeout_ms/include_impact are replayed so the rebased preview reproduces the original preflight contract exactly.

Missing imports default to warn (load succeeds and reports them), can fail closed with missing_imports=error, or can be explicitly silenced. A sibling catalog-v001.xml next to a local-file document first resolves its imports to local files (offline), like Protégé's own File ▸ Open. Note: a load is not an applyChange edit, so it does NOT join the shared undo stack — undo_change cannot revert it. Pass keep_active=true to load the document (e.g. to resolve an import) WITHOUT changing your current active edit target.

tools.description: Classify a semantic diff while retaining diff_ontologies as the fast exact axiom primitive. mode=asserted (default) reports ontology/import/ontology-annotation changes, added and removed entities by type, unique exact-label rename candidates (never automatic rewrites), per-entity annotation/lifecycle/replacement deltas, asserted axioms grouped by type and affected IRI, and a conservative compatibility classification (any logical axiom added or removed is potentially_breaking). mode=inferred|both adds the inferred-diff-v1 entailment set, computed by one explicitly recorded reasoner over both flattened sides: consistency, class satisfiability, named-class subsumption and equivalence closure deltas, named individual types, and candidate-bounded disjointness (asserted DisjointClasses/DisjointUnion candidates only); property hierarchies, characteristics, and assertions are machine-readably excluded, and every category fails closed with an error rather than an empty result. With policy_path, the module_ownership policy delta (modules[].owned_namespaces) and member-level CQ/invariant/SHACL/governance stage_deltas are also reported (the governance delta is scope: policy_rules_only — rule-driven annotation/lifecycle/waiver checks per side, not run_project_qc's intrinsic or module/import governance checks); errored inferred or stage-delta evidence forces potentially_breaking. Unresolved right_document imports are reported and, with include_imports, force potentially_breaking instead of diffing a silently truncated closure.

tools.description: Read-only SYNTACTIC impact analysis of a change. Analyzes exactly one input form: change_set_id (a cached preview from preview_change_set or create_terms/create_properties preview=true — its stored normalized delta, with the preview's base_revision echoed; reference scans run over the current workspace) OR an asserted diff pair (left, default active, against a loaded right ontology or a privately loaded right_document, like diff_ontologies; reference scans run over the compared ontologies' union, independent of whatever is active). Reports, each with exact counts and bounded samples (limit): directly_affected (every IRI in the delta axioms' signatures — including annotation subjects/IRI values — with per-IRI added/removed axiom counts, plus owning-module attribution via the policy's modules[].owned_namespaces when policy_path is given, else available:false), referencing_axioms (in-scope axioms that mention an affected IRI but are NOT part of the delta), downstream_terms (a bounded breadth-first co-occurrence sweep from the affected entities, analysis=syntactic, with disclosed depth/size caps and search_truncated), foreign_reaxiomatization (delta axioms whose SUBJECT entity is declared in an imported closure member rather than an analyzed root ontology — the import-layering notion of validate_governance; both compared sides' closures contribute in the pair form), deprecated_terms_in_use (owl:deprecated=true terms referenced by the delta or its referencing axioms), validation_references (plain-substring, match=textual occurrences of affected IRIs in the policy-resolved invariants/SHACL/CQ assets and the in-workspace CQ stores; available:false without policy_path), public_api_terms (available:false — policy v1 does not yet declare public API terms), and external_mappings (available:false — mapping management is not available in this release). The whole result is analysis=syntactic: it proves NO logical impact, and impact driven by an inferred (reasoner-computed) delta is deliberately deferred — only the asserted projection of a change is analyzed; run semantic_diff mode=inferred|both for entailment-level evidence. include_imports widens both the pair diff scope and the reference scan; the analyzed change-set entry is claimed for the duration of the (read-only) analysis and remains cached afterwards.

tools.description: Explain WHY a structured axiom is entailed: return one or more justifications (minimal sets of asserted axioms that together entail it). Minimal justifications are computed for these axiom_type values: subclass_of, equivalent_classes, disjoint_classes, class_assertion, object_property_assertion, data_property_assertion, negative_object_property_assertion, negative_data_property_assertion, same_individual, different_individuals, object_property_domain, object_property_range, data_property_domain, data_property_range. For any OTHER axiom_type (e.g. a property-hierarchy or property-characteristic entailment) it falls back to confirming whether the axiom is entailed and returning the asserted axioms that mention the same entities as structural context (not a minimal justification). To explain why a class C is unsatisfiable, use axiom_type=class_assertion with class=C and any individual, or subclass_of with sub=C, super="owl:Nothing". Requires a reasoner (see list_reasoners / set_reasoner).

annotations.description: Optional axiom annotations (array of {property, value | value_iri, lang, datatype}); reconstructs reified owl:Axiom blocks.

datatype.description: Optional datatype IRI/name for a typed literal value.

lang.description: Optional language tag for a literal value, e.g. 'en'.

property.description: Annotation property: 'rdfs:label', 'rdfs:comment', or an IRI/name (default rdfs:label).

value.description: Literal text value (omit if value_iri is given).

value_iri.description: IRI-valued annotation: an entity name/IRI or absolute IRI (alternative to value).

axiom_type.description: subclass_of, equivalent_classes, disjoint_classes, disjoint_union, class_assertion, object_property_assertion, data_property_assertion, negative_object_property_assertion, negative_data_property_assertion, same_individual, different_individuals, sub_object_property_of, sub_data_property_of, sub_property_chain_of, equivalent_object_properties, equivalent_data_properties, disjoint_object_properties, disjoint_data_properties, inverse_object_properties, transitive_object_property, functional_object_property, inverse_functional_object_property, symmetric_object_property, asymmetric_object_property, reflexive_object_property, irreflexive_object_property, functional_data_property, has_key, object_property_domain, object_property_range, data_property_domain, data_property_range, annotation_assertion, sub_annotation_property_of, annotation_property_domain, annotation_property_range, declaration, datatype_definition

chain.description: sub_property_chain_of: ordered object property list (each a name/IRI, or an inverse link inverse(P) / ObjectInverseOf(P))

class.description: class_assertion / disjoint_union / has_key: class — name, IRI or Manchester class expression

classes.description: equivalent_classes / disjoint_classes / disjoint_union: classes — names, IRIs or Manchester class expressions

datatype.description: data_property_assertion / annotation_assertion: optional datatype IRI/name; datatype_definition: defined datatype IRI/name

domain.description: object_property_domain / data_property_domain: domain class expression; annotation_property_domain: domain IRI

entity_type.description: declaration: class | object_property | data_property | annotation_property | individual | datatype

lang.description: data_property_assertion / annotation_assertion: optional language tag

max.description: Maximum number of justifications to compute (default 3; 0 = all).

properties.description: equivalent_/disjoint_object|data_properties: property IRI/name list; has_key: object/data property IRI/name list

property.description: *_property_assertion / property characteristic / sub_*_property_of / *_property_domain|range / annotation_* / has_key seed: property IRI/name

range.description: object_property_range: range class expression; data_property_range / datatype_definition: datatype IRI/name or a Manchester-syntax data range such as "xsd:integer[>= 0]" or "{1, 2, 3}"; annotation_property_range: range IRI

sub.description: subclass_of: subclass — name, IRI or Manchester class expression

super.description: subclass_of: superclass — name, IRI or Manchester class expression

super_property.description: sub_object_property_of / sub_data_property_of / sub_property_chain_of / sub_annotation_property_of: super property IRI/name

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in ms for the explanation search (default 60000).

value.description: data_property_assertion / annotation_assertion: literal value

value_iri.description: annotation_assertion: IRI-valued annotation (entity name/IRI or absolute IRI; alternative to value)

tools.name: get_explanations

tools.description: Explain WHY the ontology is INCONSISTENT: find a set of asserted logical axioms that together cause the contradiction. The result's 'minimal' flag reports whether the set was fully minimized within the time budget (false = still jointly inconsistent, but reduced-not-minimal). Runs the selected reasoner over a private copy of the imports closure (off the UI thread; the live reasoner state is untouched). If the ontology is consistent it says so. Use after run_reasoner reports INCONSISTENT — the other explanation/query tools cannot run over an inconsistent ontology.

timeout_ms.description: Time budget in ms for the whole search (default 60000). On expiry the current still-inconsistent axiom set is returned with minimal=false.

tools.name: explain_inconsistency

tools.description: Run a Protégé DL Query: given a Manchester-syntax class expression, return the reasoner's equivalent classes, subclasses, superclasses, and instances. 'relation' limits the result (equivalent | subclasses | superclasses | instances | all, default all); 'direct' limits sub/super/instance results to direct ones (default true). Caveat: for a COMPLEX (anonymous) class expression with direct=false, some reasoners — notably ELK — can return an INCOMPLETE set of sub/superclasses, omitting the DIRECT level (Protégé's own DL Query tab shows the same); the response then carries a 'warning'. Set complete=true to reconstruct the exhaustive set (the reasoner's direct results unioned with each direct class's transitive descent, which every reasoner computes reliably for named classes), or classify with a DL reasoner (e.g. HermiT). Call run_reasoner first.

complete.description: For a complex (anonymous) expression with direct=false, reconstruct the exhaustive sub/superclass set (direct + named-class descent) instead of the raw reasoner call, working around reasoners (e.g. ELK) that under-report complex-expression queries (default false).

direct.description: Direct results only for sub/super/instances (default true).

query.description: Manchester-syntax class expression, e.g. "hasOwner some Person" or "Animal and (hasOwner some Person)".

relation.description: equivalent | subclasses | superclasses | instances | all (default all).

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in ms for the query (default 60000).

tools.name: execute_dl_query

tools.description: List every reasoner factory installed in Protégé and mark the one currently selected. Factories with the same display name remain separate so their ids can disambiguate set_reasoner; then call run_reasoner to classify.
tools.name: list_reasoners

tools.description: Select the reasoner Protégé will use, by id or name (see list_reasoners). A version-less name (e.g. 'HermiT') resolves against the installed reasoners and is used only when it matches exactly ONE — zero or several matches fail, with ambiguous candidates listed as name [factory id]; a full display name (e.g. 'HermiT 1.4.3.456') or factory id must match exactly. Policy reasoning.reasoner uses the same name-resolution rule but is name-only; semantic_diff also accepts ids. This does not classify — call run_reasoner afterwards.

reasoner.description: Reasoner id or name (see list_reasoners). A version-less name must resolve to exactly one installed reasoner; a full display name pins an exact version.

tools.name: set_reasoner

tools.description: Run a SPARQL 1.1 query over the active ontology and its imports closure, using an embedded Jena ARQ engine. Supports the read query forms SELECT, ASK, CONSTRUCT and DESCRIBE; SPARQL UPDATE and SERVICE are rejected (edits go through the write tools; no network access). Prefixes declared in the ontology (plus rdf/rdfs/owl/xsd) are auto-prepended, so queries can use them without their own PREFIX lines. By default the query sees the ASSERTED triples (like Protégé's SPARQL Query tab); set include_inferred=true to first materialise the active reasoner's inferences (run_reasoner first — this runs on the UI thread and can be slow on a large ABox). 'limit' caps the rows (SELECT) or triples (CONSTRUCT/DESCRIBE) returned (default 1000).

include_inferred.description: Materialise the active reasoner's inferred axioms before querying (default false; requires a classified reasoner; runs on the UI thread).

limit.description: Max rows (SELECT) or triples (CONSTRUCT/DESCRIBE) to return (default 1000).

query.description: A SPARQL 1.1 query (SELECT, ASK, CONSTRUCT, or DESCRIBE).

timeout_ms.description: Overall time budget in ms, covering both the snapshot/inference step and the query evaluation (default 120000).

tools.name: sparql_query

tools.description: Discover the queryable vocabulary for AUTHORING a SPARQL query over the active ontology (its imports closure by default — the same graph sparql_query sees). Returns the prefix map (plus a ready-to-paste PREFIX block), and capped, sorted lists of classes, object/data properties (with their domains and ranges), named individuals and datatypes — each with a CURIE (e.g. ex:Widget) and full IRI — and a set of ready-to-run example queries built from the ontology's own terms. Use 'keyword' to focus on a sub-topic. sparql_query auto-prepends these prefixes, so you can use the CURIEs directly. This is asserted structure; for reasoner-derived triples query with include_inferred=true.

include_examples.description: Include example queries grounded in the ontology's own terms (default true).

include_imports.description: Include terms from the imports closure (default true; sparql_query queries the closure).

include_individuals.description: Include a sample of named individuals (default true).

keyword.description: Only include classes/properties/individuals whose label or IRI contains this text (case-insensitive). Use to focus on a sub-topic.

timeout_ms.description: Time budget in ms for gathering the vocabulary on the UI thread (default 120000; raise for very large imports closures).

tools.name: sparql_schema

tools.description: Check a SPARQL query BEFORE running it (it is parsed, not executed, unless dry_run=true). Reports whether it parses, the query form, the projected variables, and whether sparql_query would accept it ('executable' — a read query with no SERVICE). The ontology's prefixes are auto-prepended just as sparql_query does, so a query that uses declared CURIEs validates without its own PREFIX lines. 'unknown_terms' lists IRIs used in the query (graph patterns, property paths, VALUES, CONSTRUCT template, DESCRIBE targets) that are NOT declared in the ontology — usually a typo or a term from another vocabulary; catch these before running. A syntax error is reported as valid=false with the engine's message, not as a tool error. Set dry_run=true to also run it with a small LIMIT and return a sample.

dry_run.description: Also execute the query with a small LIMIT to confirm it runs and return a sample of results (default false).

timeout_ms.description: Time budget for the dry run in ms (default 120000).

tools.name: sparql_validate

tools.description: Audit the active ontology for modelling-quality issues (not logical consistency — use run_reasoner for that). Runs structural checks and reports, per check, a count, sample offenders, and a fix suggestion. Checks: missing_label, missing_definition, duplicate_label, multiple_labels, deprecated_in_use, undeclared_entity, property_missing_domain, property_missing_range, self_subclass, subclass_cycle, isolated_class. Imported terms (declared upstream) are not flagged for missing label/definition/domain/range when auditing the active ontology alone; set include_imports=true to audit the whole imports closure. Pass 'checks' to run a subset. These are modelling-quality checks only; set with_reasoner=true to also include the reasoner's consistency / unsatisfiable-class verdict (a clean audit is NOT proof of logical consistency).

checks.description: Subset of check ids to run (default all).

include_imports.description: Audit the imports closure too (default false).

timeout_ms.description: Time budget in ms before the call returns a timeout error (default 60000). The structural checks run on the model thread and are not interrupted mid-run, so this bounds the caller's wait, not the on-thread work itself.

with_reasoner.description: Also report the reasoner's consistency / unsatisfiable classes (uses the already-classified reasoner; run_reasoner first for a current verdict). Default false.

tools.name: validate_ontology

tools.description: Audit the active ontology against PROJECT GOVERNANCE rules (complements validate_ontology's generic quality checks and run_reasoner's logic checks). Checks: (1) owl_profile — OWL 2 profile conformance (default DL; or EL/QL/RL; 'none'/'Full' skips), reporting the axioms that leave the profile; (4) check_ownership (default true) — the active module must not assert logical axioms about IMPORTED terms (import-layering / module ownership) — both run BY DEFAULT; (2) required_namespaces / iri_pattern — every owned entity's IRI must start with one of the namespaces and/or match the regex; and (3) required_annotations — every owned class/property must carry each listed annotation property (use 'label' and 'definition' for rdfs:label / any definition property) — are opt-in. Owned = declared in the audited scope, not purely imported. Set include_imports=true to audit the whole imports closure as owned.

check_ownership.description: Flag logical axioms in the active ontology whose subject is an imported (upstream) term — an import-layering violation. Default true.

include_imports.description: Treat the whole imports closure as owned and audit it too (default false: only the active ontology's own terms).

iri_pattern.description: Owned entity IRIs must match this Java regular expression (optional; applied to the full IRI).

owl_profile.description: OWL 2 profile to check conformance against: DL (default), EL, QL, RL. Pass 'none' or 'Full' to skip the profile check.

required_annotations.description: Annotation properties every owned class/property must carry: an IRI/CURIE/name, or the specials 'label' (rdfs:label) and 'definition' (rdfs:comment / skos:definition / any *definition property). Optional.

required_namespaces.description: Owned entity IRIs must start with one of these namespace prefixes (optional; e.g. your ontology's term namespace).

timeout_ms.description: Time budget in ms before the call returns a timeout error (default 60000). The checks run on the model thread and are not interrupted mid-run, so this bounds the caller's wait, not the work.

tools.name: validate_governance

tools.description: Add or update (by id) a competency question — a SPARQL query plus an expected result that run_competency_questions later re-checks. Give the 'query' (SELECT or ASK) and, recommended, the natural-language 'text'. 'expected' is the pass condition: nonEmpty (default) | empty | 'count OP N' (OP one of >=,<=,==,>,<); EXACT_ROWS is authored directly in a sidecar-manifest. 'convention' chooses the store (robot-sparql-dir = the default *.rq writer for ROBOT/CI interop | sidecar-manifest = a full-fidelity JSON file | ontology-annotations = stored inside the ontology, the fallback when it is unsaved); omit it to follow an existing store. This writes a file (or an ontology annotation) and echoes where.

convention.description: robot-sparql-dir | sidecar-manifest | ontology-annotations (optional; omit to follow an existing store, else defaults to robot-sparql-dir, or ontology-annotations when the ontology is unsaved).

expected.description: Pass condition: nonEmpty (default) | empty | 'count OP N'.

id.description: Stable id within the store (optional; an auto CQ-N is minted if omitted).

include_inferred.description: Also run over the reasoner's inferred triples when the suite runs (default true).

query.description: Executable SPARQL 1.1 query — SELECT or ASK.

query_lang.description: Query language — only 'sparql' is supported (default sparql).

tools.name: add_competency_question

tools.description: List every competency question found across all storage conventions (robot-sparql-dir *.rq files, a sidecar-manifest JSON, and ontology annotations), each tagged with its 'convention'. Reports 'conventions_found' and any 'skipped' entries that could not be parsed (malformed input is isolated, never fatal).
tools.name: list_competency_questions

tools.description: Remove a competency question by id. Pass 'convention' to disambiguate when the same id exists in more than one store; otherwise the single store holding it is used.

convention.description: robot-sparql-dir | sidecar-manifest | ontology-annotations (optional; required only when the id exists in several stores).

id.description: The competency question id to remove.

tools.name: remove_competency_question

tools.description: Re-run the competency-question suite against the active ontology and report, per CQ, whether it still passes — a regression check for curation edits. Each CQ's query runs over a shared point-in-time snapshot (asserted triples, plus the reasoner's inferences for CQs with include_inferred=true when a classified reasoner is available). Judged by its expected result (nonEmpty / empty / count / exactRows). Filter with 'ids' or 'convention'; 'fail_on'=any makes the overall 'gate' fail if any CQ fails (default none = report only). Caveats (open-world EMPTY, truncated results/inferences) are surfaced, never silent.

convention.description: Only run CQs from this convention (default: all detected).

ids.description: Only run these CQ ids (default: all).

tools.name: run_competency_questions

tools.description: Run project-defined SPARQL INVARIANTS over the active ontology — patterns that must NEVER appear (like ROBOT 'verify'). Each queries[] item is a SPARQL SELECT/ASK whose results are VIOLATIONS: any returned row (or ASK true) flags it, at the item's severity (error | warn | info, default error). The overall 'gate' fails when a violation reaches the 'fail_on' severity (none | info | warn | error, default error). Queries run over a shared snapshot (asserted, or the reasoner's inferences for items with include_inferred=true); UPDATE/SERVICE are rejected. Violations are reported as raw SPARQL bindings (a persisted invariant 'profile' is reserved for a later release).

fail_on.description: Gate severity: none | info | warn | error (default error).

profile.description: Persisted invariant set (reserved for a later release; use inline queries[]).

queries.description: The invariants to check; each item's results are violations.

include_inferred.description: Run over the reasoner's inferred triples (default false).

sparql.description: A SPARQL SELECT or ASK whose results are VIOLATIONS (a returned row / ASK true means the forbidden pattern is present). CONSTRUCT/DESCRIBE are rejected — a graph-producing form is not a detector; use sparql_query for those.

tools.name: verify_ontology

tools.description: Validate the active ontology (its imports-closure RDF) against a SHACL shapes graph using the embedded Apache Jena SHACL engine. Provide the shapes inline as Turtle in 'shapes', or a LOCAL file path in 'shapes_path' (remote fetch is disabled for offline safety). By default validation runs over the ASSERTED triples (like sparql_query); set include_inferred=true to first materialise the active reasoner's inferences (run_reasoner first). Reports 'conforms' plus, per validation result, the focus node, result path, value, severity (Violation/Warning/Info), source shape, constraint component and message. This is the SHACL counterpart to verify_ontology's SPARQL invariants; use it for shape-based data-quality checks (cardinality, datatype, value/class constraints).

include_inferred.description: Validate over the active reasoner's inferred triples (default false; requires a classified reasoner — run_reasoner first).

shapes.description: SHACL shapes graph as Turtle text (inline). Either this or 'shapes_path' is required.

shapes_path.description: Path to a LOCAL SHACL shapes document (Turtle/RDF-XML/etc.; format inferred from the extension). Alternative to 'shapes'.

timeout_ms.description: Time budget in ms, applied to BOTH the data snapshot (on the model thread) and the SHACL validation itself (default 120000).

tools.name: shacl_validate

tools.description: Discover and return the effective version-controlled ontology project policy. Discovery order is an explicit local policy_path, then .protege-mcp/project.yaml walking from the active ontology document toward its parent roots. YAML is parsed strictly, validated against policy schema v1, defaulted deterministically, and checked for missing/escaping assets, invalid CURIEs/regexes, active-ontology mismatch, and unavailable required reasoners. With no policy, interactive legacy behavior is unchanged and policy_loaded=false is explicit.

policy_path.description: Optional local path to project.yaml. When omitted, discover .protege-mcp/project.yaml from the active ontology document upward.

tools.name: get_project_policy

tools.description: Validate a discovered or explicit project policy before ontology QC. Returns structured schema, semantic, reasoner, and filesystem findings; duplicate YAML keys, unknown fields, missing required assets, traversal/symlink escapes, malformed regexes, unknown CURIE prefixes, a root-ontology mismatch, or a missing required reasoner make valid=false. Validation never mutates the ontology or policy file.

policy_path.description: Optional local path to project.yaml. When omitted, discover .protege-mcp/project.yaml from the active ontology document upward.

tools.name: validate_project_policy

tools.description: Run the effective project policy as a strict reproducible QC gate. Every configured required stage (reasoner, profile, governance, structural, persisted invariants, policy-selected competency questions, and one or more SHACL files) must execute against one captured ontology revision. A policy violation returns gate=fail; an invalid policy, missing asset, unavailable/wrong reasoner, malformed query/shapes, or skipped/errored required stage returns gate=error and can never pass vacuously.

lock_mode.description: Optional import-lock verification request: ignore (default), verify (compare the loaded closure against the lockfile resolved with the verify_import_lock rules — the policy-declared imports.lockfile, else beside-document imports.lock.json — skipping cleanly with a note when the default file does not exist), or required (that file-absent state becomes the imports.lock_missing error finding). With imports.mode: locked the gate verification always runs regardless; results label the lockfile_source (policy_declared or beside_document).

policy_path.description: Optional explicit local project policy; otherwise discover it.

tools.name: run_project_qc

tools.description: Generate a commented, schema-valid starter .protege-mcp/project.yaml to review and commit like source code. This scaffolds a NEW policy file (it never mutates the ontology or an existing policy in place): the required blocks (version, project_id, root_ontology, interoperability) are populated from the active ontology, safe security defaults (filesystem/network deny, unlocked imports, a named reasoner, the base QC stages) are filled in, and every asset-referencing optional block (prefixes, modules, annotations, iri_policy, lifecycle, invariants/shacl/competency_questions, imports lockfile, release) is commented out with guidance. The template names a root_artifact and RO-Crate metadata file you must still create, so it is honest that it is not valid on its own and returns a validation_hint listing what to complete; it never claims valid=true. The write honors read-only mode and the confirm-write gate, resolves the target under project_root (default beside the active document at .protege-mcp/project.yaml), and lands atomically; overwrite=false refuses an existing file with error_code policy_exists.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file at the target path. Default false (an existing file is refused with error_code policy_exists and nothing is written).

path.description: Explicit project-relative or absolute policy path to write. Default: .protege-mcp/project.yaml beside the active ontology document.

profile.description: Which example-shaped starter to emit: general (OWL/Turtle, HermiT/DL) or obo (OBO edit file, ELK/EL). Default general.

project_id.description: Project identifier written into the template. Default: derived from the active ontology IRI's last path segment, else 'my-project'.

tools.name: write_project_policy_template

tools.description: Run an aggregate quality-control gate over the active ontology and collapse it to ONE verdict. Composable stages (default reasoner + profile + structural): 'interoperability' (project-policy RO-Crate contract plus W3C RDFC-1.0 root-dataset fingerprint), 'reasoner' (consistency + no unsatisfiable classes), 'profile' (OWL 2 profile conformance, owl_profile default DL), 'structural' (validate_ontology's modelling-quality checks), 'governance' (IRI/annotation/import-layering project rules), 'invariants' (verify_ontology-style SPARQL invariants — pass them in 'invariants'), 'cqs' (the competency-question suite), and 'shacl' (validate against the SHACL shapes supplied in 'shacl_shapes'/'shacl_shapes_path'). Every stage, including reasoning and inferred queries, runs against one isolated shared snapshot. A stage whose backing data is absent (no selected reasoner, no invariants, no CQs, no SHACL shapes) is skipped with a reason in legacy mode. Pass policy_path to run the strict project-policy workflow, where any missing required stage is an error. The overall 'gate' fails when the worst stage reaches 'fail_on' (none | warn | error, default error).

error_on_missing_required.description: Fail closed when a required/requested stage cannot run.

fail_on.description: Gate severity: none | warn | error (default error).

sparql.description: A SPARQL SELECT/ASK whose results are violations.

iri_pattern.description: Governance: Java regex for owned entity IRIs.

lock_mode.description: Optional import-lock verification request, honored on the strict policy branch (with policy_path): ignore (default), verify (compare the loaded closure against the lockfile resolved with the verify_import_lock rules — the policy-declared imports.lockfile, else beside-document imports.lock.json — skipping cleanly with a note when the default file does not exist), or required (that file-absent state becomes the imports.lock_missing error finding). With imports.mode: locked the gate verification always runs regardless; results label the lockfile_source. Without policy_path the legacy inline gate performs no lock verification, so verify/required is refused with an explicit error, never silently ignored.

owl_profile.description: OWL 2 profile for the profile stage: DL (default), EL, QL, RL.

policy_path.description: Optional project policy path; delegates to strict project QC.

required_stages.description: Stages that must complete; missing/skipped/error becomes gate=error.

shacl_shapes.description: SHACL shapes graph as Turtle (inline) for the 'shacl' stage.

shacl_shapes_path.description: Local file path to a SHACL shapes document for the 'shacl' stage.

stages.description: Subset of: interoperability, reasoner, profile, governance, structural, invariants, cqs, shacl (default reasoner, profile, structural; interoperability requires project policy).

timeout_ms.description: Time budget in ms for the SPARQL and SHACL stages (default 120000).

tools.name: run_qc_suite

tools.description: Read-only release gate over the active ontology: runs the strict project-policy QC gate, then the release-only checks and reports what prepare_release WOULD produce, writing nothing. On top of QC it verifies import provenance (under network=deny — the default — every closure member must be backed by an authorized local file, else an imports.remote_backed error; network=allow keeps them as a recorded network_caveat), the version IRI (release.require_version_iri), a verified serialization round trip in release.format (release.require_clean_round_trip), fingerprint stability (a session_only fingerprint blocks a stable manifest), and an optional ASSERTED baseline_manifest comparison. The overall gate is error > fail > pass. Returns gate, findings, resolved_imports, round_trip, baseline, a manifest_preview (or manifest_available:false with a reason) and a bounded reports_preview; timestamps read PREVIEW because prepare_release stamps the real created_at.

baseline_manifest.description: Optional path to a prior release manifest.json to compare against (asserted-axiom diff only; inferred baseline diff is deferred). Read with project containment.

limit.description: Maximum samples/findings per stage and in the report excerpt (default 50).

lock_mode.description: Import-lock verification: ignore (default), verify when a lock exists, or required (missing lock is an error). A locked policy always verifies.

network.description: Provenance posture for remote-backed closure members: deny (default — a non-local member is an imports.remote_backed error) or allow (kept as a recorded network_caveat). allow never overrides a policy network deny.

policy_path.description: Optional explicit local project policy; otherwise discover it.

tools.name: run_release_gate

tools.description: Produce the release bundle after run_release_gate passes. Dry-run by default: it re-runs the full release gate and, only when the gate passes, computes the verified ontology serialization, the manifest.json, the four reports (reports/qc.json, reports/qc.md, reports/qc.xml, reports/qc.sarif), the RO-Crate metadata, and reports/diff.json when a baseline is given. A gate that does not pass is refused with structured findings and NO writes. dry_run=true (the default) returns the manifest, reports and crate content inline (bounded) and writes nothing. dry_run=false honors Protégé read-only mode and the confirm-writes gate, then writes every artifact atomically into the release output directory (policy release.output_dir, or output_dir) via the containment-enforcing artifact store, each with its sha256 recorded in the manifest. No network access is ever performed.

baseline_manifest.description: Optional path to a prior release manifest.json to compare against (asserted diff only); written as reports/diff.json when supplied.

created_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp stamped into the manifest and crate for reproducibility. When omitted and dry_run=false the system clock is read once; a dry run uses a PREVIEW placeholder instead.

dry_run.description: When true (default) compute and return every artifact inline but write nothing. Pass false to commit the artifacts to the output directory.

limit.description: Maximum samples/findings per stage and in the report excerpt (default 50).

lock_mode.description: Import-lock verification: ignore (default), verify when a lock exists, or required (missing lock is an error). A locked policy always verifies.

network.description: Provenance posture for remote-backed closure members: deny (default) or allow (recorded as a caveat). allow never overrides a policy network deny.

output_dir.description: Release output directory (default the policy release.output_dir asset). Resolved with project containment; artifacts can never escape it.

policy_path.description: Optional explicit local project policy; otherwise discover it.

tools.name: prepare_release

tools.description: Explicitly export the active project's redacted, owner-only audit streams as one deterministically ordered JSON Lines artifact. Dry-run is the default and writes nothing. A committed export requires a valid discovered project policy, server administration plus project read/write capabilities, the live read-only/confirmation gates, and a project-contained output path. The export is bounded, re-redacted, and contains caller attribution, capability sets, operations, targets, gate/change summaries, confirmation references, and release-manifest links; it never includes bearer tokens, prompts, attached bodies, or ontology content.

dry_run.description: When true (default), report the intended output and write nothing. Pass false to create the export after confirmation.

output.description: Optional dedicated project-relative output matching .protege-mcp/audit-export*.jsonl (default .protege-mcp/audit-export.jsonl). Other project files cannot be overwritten.

tools.name: export_audit_log
